title: Bank of Japan MPM decision + Outlook Report (MPM Apr 27-28, 2027 — first meeting after the food consumption-tax cut takes effect)
source: NEWS: boj.or.jp 'Monetary Policy Meetings' schedule page (en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/), re-fetched raw direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 41,959 bytes) and column-parsed out of the HTML by this session. The 'Table : 2027' row parses as ['Apr. 27 (Tues.), 28 (Wed.)', 'Apr. 28 (Wed.)', 'May 12 (Wed.)', 'June 16 (Wed.)'] against the header 'Date of MPM | Outlook Report (The Bank's View) | Summary of Opinions | MPM Minutes' — the dated Outlook column is the primary evidence that this IS an Outlook Report meeting. Filed estimate on three counts, identical to the sibling BoJ entries: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has FED: and no slot for any other central bank, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and a schedule published ~20 months ahead is the most movable kind
notes: Proposed during the boj-decision-2027-01-22 initial research (2026-09-05) for one specific reason: it is the FIRST MPM after Japan's food consumption-tax cut takes effect on 2027-04-01 (japan-food-tax-cut-2027-04-01, estimate — 8% to 1% for two years, announced by PM Takaichi, LDP-approved and pending Diet passage as of 2026-08-07 per News On Japan and vatcalc.com), and the first Outlook Report that must project a fiscal year whose CPI carries the cut for its entire span. FY2027 runs 2027-04-01 to 2028-03-31; the cut covers all of it. The BoJ's July-2026 Outlook put the FY2027 core-CPI median at +2.4% (revised up from +2.3% in April) and FY2028 at +2.0%, and the bank's standing projection footnote strips 'the effects of consumption tax HIKES' — wording written for 2014 and 2019, not for a cut. Whether that convention is extended to a cut is decided in January 2027 and first tested against realised data here. SAME CHANNEL, SAME CAVEAT AS THE OTHER BoJ ENTRIES: yen funding and global term premium are both second-order for a US equity book and both already owned by the FOMC ledgers; symbols is empty and no house playbook is rates- or FX-keyed. Second reason this venue matters: it is one of only TWO MPMs inside Q2 2027 (with Jun. 10-11, same primary table), which is the window Reuters' 2026-07-23 poll found '70% of economists anticipate the BoJ to hike rates to at least 1.50%' in — so the consensus level target has two venues and this is the first. INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-05 (docs/research/events/boj-decision-2027-04-28.md) REFUTES part of the framing above and adds three venue-specific structures. (1) The consumption-tax footnote cited here and in four sibling ledgers DOES NOT EXIST in the Outlook Report: this session installed pypdf and extracted five Bank's View reports (gor2601a/2604a/2607a/2404a/2004a) plus two full texts, and the forecast table's notes are 1-3 only (medians, range construction, past policy decisions) with ZERO occurrences of 'tax' anywhere, including the April 2020 report published six months after the 2019 hike. With no convention to extend, booking the drag is the more live branch, not the less. The Bank does add ad-hoc notes though (April 2026 Note 4: 'The CPI figures for fiscal 2025 are actual values'), which is what makes it a registrable binary (FT-boj-decision-2027-04-28-1). The July-2026 medians quoted above ARE correct, now read verbatim off the Bank's own table: FY2027 +2.4 (up from +2.3 in April 2026), FY2028 +2.0. (2) CORRECTION to 'first tested against realised data here' — it is not. The APRIL Outlook is where the projection horizon extends by a fiscal year (Jan 2026 = FY2025/26/27; Apr 2026 = FY2025/26/27/28, the new row carrying no January comparison line), so April 2027 is the first document to publish FY2029 — and since the cut runs 2027-04-01 to 2029-03-31, a y/y index carries the drag in FY2027, nothing in FY2028, and the UNWIND in FY2029. That is the venue's real signature: a V across three consecutive rows in the first table that must print the third. The meeting itself sees no national post-cut CPI (that trails into May), which is why boj-decision-2027-06-11 was proposed alongside. (3) The April 2027 FOMC is Apr 27-28 — the IDENTICAL two days, per federalreserve.gov's own calendar — with no SEP, while Tokyo is closed 2027-04-29 for Showa Day, so attribution across that window is not recoverable; filed as fomc-2027-04-28, which the +/-5-day corridor had entirely missed. And the same slot one year earlier (k260428a.pdf, 2026-04-28) HELD at 0.75% by 6-3 with three dissents to hike, the hike landing seven weeks later at the non-Outlook June meeting — on a complete 2025-2026 window the Bank moved at 1 of 7 Outlook meetings versus 2 of 6 ordinary ones (n=3, thin; registered as FT-boj-decision-2027-04-28-2, not asserted). Stance unchanged: stand aside, no position.
